entries.source: Set the top-left corner of this image on the output canvas. X and Y are whole pixels, starting at zero. Other images keep their current positions. Overlap is allowed here; images imported later are drawn on top. The canvas expands to include all placed images. Crops and sizes stay unchanged.
entries.target: A=sanke noka a=nuye uske or ta, tan noka tuyka ta ka tan noka harkisama ta ka an sikkew anu yan. X ka Y ka, 「0, 1, 2, 3, …」 or wa a=numke cipiskip ne; pixel ani, 0 wano a=piski. Mosma noka a=ari uske anak a=sinnare ka somo ki. Te ta noka a=ukaomare yakka pirka; oka ta a=omare noka anak hoski a=omare noka ka ta a=nuye. A=ari noka opitta anak noka a=nuye uske onnay ta oka kuni, noka a=nuye uske poro. A=tuye uske ka noka kor pororu ka a=sinnare ka somo ki.
entries.note: The revised opening closes the sole remaining prior hold. This decision covers this exact complete value, including all unchanged later clauses, not a proposed splice or additional rewrite.
connected_language_assessment: I assessed each complete paragraph, including its first-command object/destination relation and the following numerical, invariance, ordering, expansion and crop/size clauses. Acceptance is not inferred solely from word matches, script agreement or the earlier local-clause decisions.

The previous structural hold is closed by the actual revised string: both image-relative locations are overt, their shared existence predicate occurs before one corner head, and the former comma-separated post-head pe apposition is gone.

A separate local antecedent is no longer needed for harkisama. Both tan noka occurrences identify the same deictic image. A generic sikkew can be identified by its restrictive locative relative; a possessed sikkewe head is not compulsory for this construction.

The earlier independently supported meanings of the unchanged sentences remain supported after reading them in this revised paragraph. No evidence-based reason was found to reopen the numerical-membership, position-invariance, permission, layer-order, explicit-container, purpose or enlargement decisions.

The explicit repeated image phrase is conservative and somewhat heavy technical prose. This affects idiom confidence, but does not introduce a competing command or unresolved referent in the stated image context.

clause_audit.source_unit: Set the top-left corner of this image on the output canvas.
clause_audit.target_language_analysis: The initial output drawing-place locative is the destination of anu yan. Inside its object NP, the two explicit tan noka referents each precede their own directional relational noun. The complete upper-edge and left-side locatives carry repeated additive ka and precede a single an predicate, whose postposed nominal head is sikkew. Thus one corner satisfies both restrictions. In the rectangular-image UI context this is its top-left corner, not two corners or the canvas top-left. The conceptual corner head does not leave a possessed-head antecedent unresolved.
clause_audit.inference_limit: A productive composition applied to image geometry; not an independently attested traditional top-left software idiom.

clause_audit.source_unit: X and Y are whole pixels, starting at zero.
clause_audit.target_language_analysis: Repeated ka applies the chosen-number predicate to both axes. Selection from the explicit 0, 1, 2, 3, … progression establishes unit-step nonnegative numeric membership rather than equating an axis to the whole list. The pixel ani clause gives the unit and 0 wano a=piski establishes the zero origin. No equality of X and Y is required. The Help does not need to repeat the separate validation maximum.
clause_audit.inference_limit: Source-plus-selection syntax is attested; applying it to a written mathematical domain and using pixel as a unit are transparent modern extensions.

clause_audit.source_unit: Other images keep their current positions.
clause_audit.target_language_analysis: Mosma noka a=ari uske identifies the placement locations of the other images. Their topic is followed by the negative-change predicate a=sinnare ka somo ki. This directly describes position invariance, not a prohibition on the user or a claim that other images are absent.
clause_audit.inference_limit: The locations are understood as their existing placement locations in this operation; no conflicting temporal reference is introduced.

clause_audit.target_language_analysis: Te ta restricts the statement to here. Ukaomare supplies putting items over one another, with the attested yakka pirka permission frame.
clause_audit.inference_limit: Application of physical overlap to image layers is technical but preserves the relation.

clause_audit.source_unit: Images imported later are drawn on top.
clause_audit.target_language_analysis: The later imported images are the topic; the earlier imported images provide the explicit locative referent for ka ta before a=nuye. The resulting surface/layer relation gives later-on-top ordering without reversing import time. This surface ka is distinct from upper-edge tuyka in the opening.
clause_audit.inference_limit: Import is the published modern omare extension. The surface-object preference noted in Tamura is balanced by attested content-drawing/writing examples in the published dictionary entries.

clause_audit.source_unit: The canvas expands to include all placed images.
clause_audit.target_language_analysis: A=ari noka opitta topicalizes all placed images. Noka a=nuye uske immediately before onnay is the explicit container; the plural placed images are the subject of oka inside the kuni purpose clause. The repeated drawing-place NP is the subject of poro in the main clause, so the canvas grows to contain the images, rather than resizing the images.
clause_audit.inference_limit: Drawing place is descriptive canvas terminology. Poro supports becoming larger; a different technical enlargement verb is not required.

clause_audit.target_language_analysis: Repeated ka coordinates the cut/crop places and the images’ size under the same explicit negative-change predicate. The final clause coheres with the preceding canvas-only enlargement: canvas growth does not imply image resizing or changed cropping.
clause_audit.inference_limit: Crop/place is descriptive and pororu is a published coined size term; neither is represented as community-standard terminology.

prior_hold_resolution.evidence: Two complete explicit image-relative locatives precede one an sikkew relative-clause head; the former post-head apposition and implicit left-side possessor are removed.

remaining_uncertainty: Modern technical terms and the image-geometry application are transparent compositional choices, not all established dictionary software idioms.
No runtime/font/layout or installed-build check was performed.

paired_script_review.result: No lexical, grammatical, numeric, identifier or punctuation divergence was detected between the complete Latin and Kana paragraphs.
notable_checks: Both explicit tan noka / タン ノカ references and both ta ka / タ カ pairs are preserved.
An / アン and conceptual sikkew / シッケウ are preserved; there is no retained sikkewe / シッケウェ.
Person-prefix distinctions, including a=ari / アアリ versus imperative anu / アヌ, are preserved.
Final consonant and gemination forms, including cipiskip / チピㇱキㇷ゚ and harkisama / ハㇻキサマ, were compared.
X, Y, pixel, 0, unit-step enumeration, quotes, commas, semicolons and periods agree.

G1.type: Primary grammar: Tamura Suzuko, Saru Ainu dictionary grammatical overview (1996)
sections: 5(2): explicit referent before a relational noun
G1.use: An explicit noun can anchor a relational location. A locative can carry additive ka. A clause precedes the noun it modifies; singular an supplies the shared corner predicate. The new two-location relative is a productive composition of these rules, not an attested software quotation.
G1.capture_note: Fresh public HTML capture, with scripts and any transient CSRF metadata removed; hash identifies these saved sanitized bytes.
G1.reviewer_evidence: Sections 2(2–3), 4(2), 5(2–3), 6, 7 and 8 support prenominal clauses, locative-plus-additive syntax, singular/plural existence, explicit relational referents, place heads, indefinite-person forms, commands and productive derivation. Section 5(2) explicitly permits both conceptual and possessed relational forms after a noun referent.
G1.inference_boundary: The double-locative restriction of a single image corner is the independent reviewer’s compositional analysis, not a quotation from this grammar.

D9.reviewer_evidence: Harkisama is the possessed relational left-side form; the new immediately preceding tan noka supplies its referent.

D10.type: Primary published Tamura/Kayano dictionary entries, read in full relevant entries
D10.evidence: Upper end/edge, distinguished from a surface on which something is laid or drawn.
D10.reviewer_evidence: Tuyka covers an upper end/edge and is specifically distinguished from the surface noun ka. Its conceptual form may follow an explicit noun referent under the grammar’s relational-noun rule.

D11.reviewer_evidence: Sikkew denotes a physical corner, including inner or outer corners. The new unpossessed head is restricted by its entire preceding locative relative.

P1.evidence: The speaker selects a good portion of meat from a bowl. This directly attests source or wa with numke. Extending the source to a written numeric collection is the reviewer’s compositional judgment, not a claim that this example contains mathematics.

C1.type: Published modern terminology collection; primary evidence of proposals only
C1.evidence: cipiskip is published for number; omare/sanke are published computing import/export terms; pororu is explicitly a coined size term. Publication is not broad community endorsement.

D22.type: Primary published Tamura/Kayano dictionary entries, freshly fetched directly by HTTPS
D22.evidence: Singular existence/location; adverbial expressions combine with an to form a predicate. One an after both complete locatives is the intended shared predicate of the one corner head.
D22.capture_note: Extracted entry JSON for local linguistic checking; not a publishable source facsimile.
